registered_at: 2026-11-09, before any model below was trained and before any listed analysis was computed
requested_by: Author (user), 2026-11-09: differentiation = decoupling of class-agnostic hole perception from CAD class knowledge + decision-margin reliability; experiments = leave-one-class-out unknown rejection and training-residual reliability prediction

common.decision: Unchanged v1 geometry gate, peak threshold 0.15, 30 mm CAD reject (a past development setting, fixed since v1); pixel width primary; scale median of TRAIN session medians per camera
common.session_rule: majority of judged frames; tie or no judged frame = abstain
common.band: correct-decision band of each class = inside both the midpoint to each neighbouring CAD value and the 30 mm reject boundary (Table 1)

loco.question: When one registered class is removed (unregistered), are its doors rejected, including near-dimension siblings 41-50 mm away, and what does each method cost on the other doors?
loco.primary_split: fold 0 TEST (74 doors, 1,478 images) for every method

hole.detector: unchanged holes_field8_f0_s42_v2 (fold 0) and holes_field8_f{k}_s42_v3 (folds 1-4); these detectors saw one field image of class c among their 8 field training images (disclosed; the E23 doors are the evidence for detection on a class never seen in training)
hole.scale: pixel scale S refit on the split's TRAIN sessions excluding class c, same rule
hole.additional: five-fold OOF (361 doors) as well, since no retraining is needed
hole.registration: re-adding CAD c gives back the closed-set decision already reported (fold0_test_v3, extension_v3); not recomputed

cnn.runs: rgb_loco_{c}_f0_s42 and rgbe_loco_{c}_f0_s42 for the 8 classes (16 runs)
cnn.training: Same recipe as rgb_f0_s42/rgbe_f0_s42 (config/protocol.json cnn: 448, Adam 3e-4, max 40 epochs, patience 8, sqrt class weights, ReduceLROnPlateau, checkpoint by VAL session balanced accuracy) on fold-0 TRAIN sessions without class c, selected on fold-0 VAL sessions without class c; 7 outputs
cnn.threshold: same pre-specified v1 rule: confidence at the 5th percentile of the 7-class model's VAL frame confidences; accept when confidence >= threshold
cnn.registration: adding class c requires retraining with class-c data; not run

metrics.primary: per excluded class c: class-c TEST doors rejected (session abstained) by hole (30 mm) and by CNN (val threshold); known TEST doors (other 7 classes) correct / wrong / abstained under the same rule
metrics.secondary: frame-level unknown rejection; threshold-free frame AUROC of known vs unknown (CNN: max softmax; hole: minus distance to the nearest registered CAD value, gate-failed frames lowest); closed-set CNN argmax destination of class-c doors
metrics.pooled: sum over the 8 runs (each fold-0 test door is unknown in exactly one run)

margin.question: Do the TRAIN sessions, already labelled for scale calibration, predict the TEST reliability of each distance representation before deployment?
margin.train_prediction: apply the unchanged decision (train-fitted scale, 8 CAD values) to the split's TRAIN sessions: predicted door failure rate = (wrong + abstained) / train doors; frame out-of-band rate among measured frames; per-class margin utilisation U_c = max over train doors of (door median residual / band edge on its side)
margin.test_observation: existing TEST predictions (reports/fold0_test_v3, reports/extension_v3): observed door failure rate, frame out-of-band rate, per-class U_c
margin.comparison: per split and pooled (five folds: sums of train-door decisions and of test-door decisions; temporal separate); Wilson 95% intervals; descriptive agreement only
margin.disclosure: TRAIN sessions include the 8 (or 24) field images used to train the detector; S and K are fit on the same TRAIN sessions (one scalar each)

rules: No threshold, gate, CAD value or scale rule is changed after viewing any output of this protocol.
All runs and reports use new names; nothing existing is overwritten.
Seeds other than 42 and a hole detector retrained without class c are not part of this protocol.
